tldr_label: TL;DR — Trump says an Iran strike could come 'tomorrow' as Brazil votes and Europe marches

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Trump said the US could strike Iran 'maybe tomorrow' or reach a 'big, beautiful' deal; Iran says it will not let US warships near the Gulf. No strike had been reported as of Sunday morning. [[TAG:danger:strike watch]]

tldr_bullets.label: Diplomacy
tldr_bullets.body: Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, the UK, France, Germany and Italy said in Istanbul that a new attack on Iran would widen the war.

tldr_bullets.label: Brazil
tldr_bullets.body: Brazilians vote today in a runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula that final polls call a statistical tie.

tldr_bullets.label: Europe
tldr_bullets.body: More than 400,000 marched in France with nearly 1,000 detained, while clashes in Tirana injured more than 300, authorities said. [[TAG:warning:unrest spreads]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Israel locked down the West Bank after a shooting near Hebron killed two soldiers, days before Tuesday's election.

tldr_bullets.label: Ebola
tldr_bullets.body: WHO and Congo began a vaccine trial in Bunia testing whether Ervebo protects against the Bundibugyo strain, as deaths passed 4,600.

sections.title: Iran: Strike or Deal
sections.summary: Trump says strike could come 'tomorrow'; Iran bars US warships; IRGC claims two more mine hits

paragraphs.heading: Trump keeps options open
paragraphs.body: Asked about another attack, Trump said 'We're thinking about doing it, and maybe tomorrow', while saying Iran could still avert strikes with a 'big, beautiful' deal he doubted Tehran would honor, Arab Times and The Tribune reported. He declined to say whether a decision had been made. Envoy Tom Barrack said a strike could come this weekend but that the goal 'won't be regime change', Arab News and Middle East Eye reported. No strike had been reported as of Sunday morning. [[TAG:danger:decision pending]]

paragraphs.heading: Iran's warnings
paragraphs.body: IRGC chief of staff Ali Abdollahi said Iran will not allow US warships into the Persian Gulf, Al Jazeera reported. The IRGC claimed two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels hit mines on an 'unauthorized route' in the southern strait, which Anadolu and Mehr reported but no independent source confirmed. Iran's ambassador to Pakistan said Tehran remains open to the Pakistan-brokered framework, CBS News reported. [[TAG:warning:unverified claims]]

paragraphs.heading: Allies say no
paragraphs.body: Foreign ministers of Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia met their British, French, German and Italian counterparts in Istanbul; Turkey's Hakan Fidan said 'a new attack on Iran would expand the war' and 'nobody approves this at the moment', Reuters reported via US News and The Jerusalem Post. The group called for full resumption of secure passage through Hormuz.

paragraphs.heading: Hardship at home
paragraphs.body: President Masoud Pezeshkian said many Iranians are struggling to afford food because of wartime conditions, describing a state of 'neither war nor peace', AFP reported via Arab News and Gulf News.

sections.sources: Arab Times, The Tribune, Arab News, Middle East Eye, Al Jazeera, Anadolu, Mehr, CBS News, US News, The Jerusalem Post, Gulf News

sections.title: Saudi Arabia and Yemen
sections.summary: Houthis claim strikes on Riyadh airport, Yanbu, Rabigh and the East-West Pipeline

paragraphs.heading: New claims
paragraphs.body: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group hit Riyadh's King Khalid airport, an Aramco facility in Yanbu, Rabigh refinery pumping stations and the East-West Pipeline, among other targets, France 24 and The Spokesman-Review reported. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation; the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missiles aimed at Yanbu and Taif. [[TAG:warning:unconfirmed hits]]

paragraphs.heading: Aden
paragraphs.body: Yemen's Saudi-backed government said the Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at coast guard sites in Aden, France 24 reported. The fighting has shattered the UN-brokered truce of 2022.

sections.title: Israel Before the Vote
sections.summary: Hebron checkpoint attack kills two soldiers; West Bank locked down ahead of Tuesday's election

paragraphs.heading: Hebron attack
paragraphs.body: Two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed, the army said, according to The Washington Post. Israel ordered a full West Bank lockdown and cordoned off Hebron and Halhul, and Netanyahu vowed soldiers would go 'house to house', NBC News and CBS News reported. Netanyahu called the gunmen Hamas members; Hamas did not claim responsibility. [[TAG:danger:2 soldiers killed]]

paragraphs.heading: Election impact
paragraphs.body: Netanyahu cancelled Friday campaign events and said the attack was an attempt to influence the election, NPR reported. Final polls put Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar ahead of Likud but show neither bloc reaching 61 seats. Israel votes Tuesday. [[TAG:info:vote Tuesday]]

sections.sources: The Washington Post, NBC News, CBS News, Al Jazeera, NPR, Haaretz

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Kyiv reports Starlink restored; overnight drone strikes kill three in Russia's border regions

paragraphs.heading: Starlink
paragraphs.body: Kyiv said Starlink service had been restored, Al Jazeera reported, a day after Ukrainian officials disputed Trump's claim that Elon Musk had lifted the restrictions. [[TAG:success:service restored]]

paragraphs.heading: Overnight strikes
paragraphs.body: Ukrainian drone attacks killed one person in Belgorod and two in a strike on a minibus in Bryansk, and damaged an industrial site in Perm, Russian officials said, according to The Moscow Times and Anadolu. Russia said it downed 532 Ukrainian drones over 25 regions. Russian strikes injured 10 people in Kharkiv and Vinnytsia, Ukraine's emergency service said. [[TAG:danger:strikes continue]]

paragraphs.heading: Talks ahead
paragraphs.body: Russia and Ukraine say peace talks are planned for November in the UAE, Al Jazeera reported, but Global News noted Moscow still demands territory it does not fully control while Kyiv insists on guarantees against another invasion.

sections.sources: Al Jazeera, The Moscow Times, Anadolu, TRT World, Global News

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump rallies in Georgia and touts Audi plant; early votes top 24 million, up 13% on 2022

paragraphs.heading: Georgia rally
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied in Perry, Georgia, and announced that Audi will invest $4.2 billion in a manufacturing plant in Macon, Fox News and Atlanta News First reported. He was due in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday.

paragraphs.heading: Early vote surge
paragraphs.body: More than 24.3 million ballots had been cast across 45 reporting states as of Saturday, 13% above the same point in 2022, according to a tracker cited by Your News. Harris County, Texas, set midterm records for in-person early voting, ABC13 reported, and Dallas County reported a record first day, Fox 4 reported. Figures vary between trackers. sections.title: Europe in the Streets
sections.summary: 400,000 march in France, nearly 1,000 detained; Tirana clashes injure 300-plus; Italy detains 371

paragraphs.heading: France
paragraphs.body: More than 400,000 people protested across France on Saturday, over 100,000 of them in Paris, and nearly 1,000 were detained, the Interior Ministry said, according to CNN and Al Jazeera. Marches were mostly peaceful, with clashes in Paris, Marseille and Bordeaux, and several cities banned protests outright. [[TAG:warning:~1,000 detained]]

paragraphs.heading: Albania and Italy
paragraphs.body: In Tirana, authorities said more than 300 protesters and police were injured as police used tear gas and water cannon and government buildings were attacked, Al Jazeera and Euronews reported; Prime Minister Edi Rama has refused to resign. Italian police said they arrested nine people and briefly detained 371 in protests across eight cities, NPR reported. Peaceful pension and housing marches were held in Madrid and Lisbon. [[TAG:danger:300+ injured]]

paragraphs.heading: A movement
paragraphs.body: Fortune described the protests as part of a newly formed 'Oct. 17 Movement' driven by living costs, pensions, housing and education.

sections.sources: CNN, Al Jazeera, Euronews, NPR, Fortune, Bloomberg

sections.title: Brazil Votes
sections.summary: Runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula today; polls show a statistical tie

paragraphs.heading: Runoff day
paragraphs.body: Brazilians vote today in a runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party, who led the first round with 47.03%, and President Lula, who took 45.16%, CFR and Americas Quarterly reported. Final polls show a technical tie, and prediction markets give Bolsonaro about 80% odds, The Rio Times reported. Results begin after polls close at 5 p.m. Brasília time. [[TAG:info:results tonight]]

sections.title: Global Roundup
sections.summary: Ebola vaccine trial starts in Congo; Kim Jong Un makes day trip to China's Dandong

paragraphs.heading: Ebola vaccine trial
paragraphs.body: WHO and Congolese health officials began the Tumaini trial in Bunia, giving the Ervebo vaccine to high-risk contacts to test whether it protects against the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine is approved, Al Jazeera reported. Congo's outbreak has passed 9,700 cases and 4,600 deaths, Sahara Reporters reported. [[TAG:success:trial begins]]

paragraphs.heading: Kim in Dandong
paragraphs.body: Kim Jong Un made a one-day trip to Dandong across a new bridge over the Yalu River, accompanied by China's fourth-ranking leader Wang Huning, who conveyed Xi Jinping's greetings, Xinhua reported via The Japan Times and PBS. Earlier reports, citing a South Korean official, said Premier Li Qiang met him.

sections.sources: Al Jazeera, Sahara Reporters, Medical Xpress, The Japan Times, PBS, Korea Times
